skills.name: customer-inquiry-intake
skills.description: Reads a customer RFQ in whatever shape it arrived — a PDF drawing package, a 40-line spreadsheet, a portal export, a phone photo of a marked-up print, or a forwarded thread where the real requirement is four messages down — and pulls specifications, quantities and dates into one consistent intake form with every field traceable to the file and page it came from. Records how each tolerance was read and which geometry path each line takes. Reports what was never stated separately from what was stated two different ways. Checks the request against what the plant can actually build before asking the customer anything, drafts the questions back as sendable text, and returns a provisional bid/no-bid that names which unanswered question would change it. Use when someone says "an RFQ came in," "can we quote this," "should we bid this job," "read this inquiry," or "what's missing from this RFQ?"

skills.name: daily-production-report
skills.description: Produces the morning production report: output against plan by line, cell and product; OEE with availability, performance and quality shown separately; the downtime log ranked both by minutes and by frequency; scrap and downtime priced in dollars; week-over-week movers; and the exceptions needing a decision today. For each significant exception it drafts a specific reschedule or changeover move with its consequences traced, never a re-optimised day. Reads the consolidated dataset and leads with data freshness. When the plant has a floor plan on file, or attaches one, it also draws each machine's OEE, availability and downtime on a schematic of the floor. Use when someone says "morning report," "production report," "how did we do yesterday," "what's our OEE," "downtime report," "what's late," or "what do I take into the production meeting."

skills.name: data-consolidate
skills.description: Joins the plant's scheduled exports and connector data into one working dataset — ERP items (NetSuite or Infor M3), sales orders, production work orders, purchase orders, inventory, routings and closed-job operation actuals; CMMS assets and maintenance work orders; and the MES, historian, quality and planning files landing in the Microsoft 365 export folder. Keys on part number, production work order, sales order, lot, asset and supplier, classifies every key that fails to match into one of eight mismatch classes, and proposes the correction rather than reporting a count, applying nothing without a yes. Runs file-only with no connector, or connector-only with no files. Use when someone says "pull the data together," "consolidate the exports," "build the dataset," "join production to the ERP," or "why don't these numbers match," and before any reporting or quoting skill runs.

skills.name: design-space-explore
skills.description: Generates a batch of CAD variants directly in Autodesk Fusion by applying changed parameters to an engineer's existing model, never designing from scratch and never overwriting the base. Checks first whether the parameters the engineer wants to vary actually drive the model's geometry, and stops rather than generating garbage if they don't. Confirms the variant count with the engineer before generating anything. Captures mass, volume, bounding box and every other model-computed property per variant, and hands the batch off in the shape trade-study-report consumes — it does not run analysis itself. Use when someone says "explore the design space," "generate variants," "try different wall thicknesses," "run a parameter sweep," or "vary this and see what happens."

skills.description: An example user-invoked skill that demonstrates frontmatter options and the skills/<name>/SKILL.md layout

skills.name: example-skill
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks to "demonstrate skills", "show skill format", "create a skill template", or discusses skill development patterns. Provides a reference template for creating Claude Code plugin skills.

skills.name: faq
skills.description: Turn repeat questions into a pinned FAQ. Use when a champion keeps answering the same questions.

skills.name: hackathon
skills.description: Plan a hackathon, either from a team's real backlog or as open-ended creative play with Claude Code. Use when a champion wants to run a hack day or a shorter hack session.

skills.name: inspection-to-capa
skills.description: Runs the quality chain end to end: writes the nonconformance against the requirement it violates, searches history at the moment of writing to say whether this has happened before and whether the last fix held, reads sensor and inspection data on one verified timeline, proposes ranked candidate causes with evidence for and against, drafts the 8D, and produces the customer pack behind a redaction diff. Use when someone says "run the CAPA chain," "take this nonconformance through to an 8D," "inspection to CAPA," or asks for the full corrective-action workflow.

skills.name: m5-onboard
skills.description: End-to-end onboarding for a freshly-plugged-in M5Stack ESP32 device (Cardputer, Cardputer-Adv, Core, CoreS3, Stick) — detect on USB, flash UIFlow 2.0 firmware, and install the Claude Buddy MicroPython app bundle. Use whenever the user plugs in or wants to flash/provision/reset an M5Stack or ESP32 board, or says "m5-onboard go".

skills.name: mcp-integration
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks to "add MCP server", "integrate MCP", "configure MCP in plugin", "use .mcp.json", "set up Model Context Protocol", "connect external service", mentions "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} with MCP", or discusses MCP server types (SSE, stdio, HTTP, WebSocket). Provides comprehensive guidance for integrating Model Context Protocol servers into Claude Code plugins for external tool and service integration.

skills.name: ncr-writeup
skills.description: Writes the nonconformance report: what was found and measured, the specific requirement it violates cited to its document and locator, how many parts are actually suspect and why that scope rather than a narrower one, and where every one of them physically is across all five locations. Searches prior NCRs and CAPAs at the moment of writing and reports whether the earlier fix held. Where containment places parts at a customer, drafts the escape notification automatically against its contractual clock. Never asserts a requirement it cannot locate. Keeps the site's Quality Register of open NCRs up to date, and closes an NCR there when told to. Use when someone says "write up this nonconformance," "we found bad parts," "raise an NCR," "the inspector rejected this lot," "a customer is complaining about a part," or "close NCR-2026-0141."

skills.name: office-hours
skills.description: Set up and run Claude Code office hours, including the calendar event when the champion's own calendar connector allows it. Use when a champion wants a regular time for teammates to bring problems.

skills.name: patterns
skills.description: Find patterns worth sharing from recent PRs and repo history, both repeats to fix and good practices worth spreading. Use when a champion wants to know what the team should reuse or learn from.

skills.name: playground
skills.description: Creates interactive HTML playgrounds — self-contained single-file explorers that let users configure something visually through controls, see a live preview, and copy out a prompt. Use when the user asks to make a playground, explorer, or interactive tool for a topic.

skills.name: plugin-structure
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks to "create a plugin", "scaffold a plugin", "understand plugin structure", "organize plugin components", "set up plugin.json", "use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}", "add commands/agents/skills/hooks", "configure auto-discovery", or needs guidance on plugin directory layout, manifest configuration, component organization, file naming conventions, or Claude Code plugin architecture best practices.

skills.name: quote-build
skills.description: Produces the make-to-order quote from the intake form, comparable prior jobs and cost history, with every number traced to where it came from — material at the price actually paid on a named purchase order, machine hours per operation from a labelled ladder (current routing, closed-job actuals, the confirmed design, first principles) with setup and run kept apart, setup re-amortized at each quantity break, and margin on its own line. Checks the promised date against real shop load before committing to it. Revises in place when a customer counters, preserving what changed and why. Use when someone says "build the quote," "price this job," "what should we charge," "quote this RFQ," or "the customer came back on price."

skills.name: rfq-to-quote
skills.description: Runs the whole RFQ-to-quote chain end to end: reads the inquiry and its drawings, checks it against what the plant can build, drafts the questions back, returns a provisional bid/no-bid, pulls cost history, routings and closed-job actuals, builds an internal estimating model in Fusion where connected (from the drawing, a prior part's model saved as new, text specs as a ROM only, or a STEP file), derives machine hours per operation with each hour's basis labelled, and drafts the quote with its cost basis shown. Four approval gates, and the chain pauses for days while the customer answers. Use when someone says "run the RFQ chain," "take this RFQ all the way to a quote," "quote this end to end," "quote this from the drawing," or names an inquiry and asks for the full workflow.

skills.name: root-cause-capa
skills.description: Reads sensor history, inspection measurements, maintenance records and prior tickets onto one verified timeline, runs the pattern checks in code rather than by eye — SPC drift, clustering by lot, shift, operator, machine and tool change, correlation with a maintenance event — then proposes ranked candidate causal chains, each with the evidence for it, the evidence against it, and the test that would confirm or kill it. Drafts the 8D. Where the leading candidate points at purchased material, raises the supplier-caused flag that starts a sourcing action. Use when someone says "why did this happen," "root cause," "write the 8D," "investigate this nonconformance," "CAPA," or "the customer wants a corrective action report."

skills.name: routines
skills.description: Set up recurring champion routines as Claude Code scheduled tasks. Use when a champion wants work like a weekly patterns digest, a stale guidance check, or a monthly lead update to happen without kicking it off by hand.

skills.name: skill-development
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user wants to "create a skill", "add a skill to plugin", "write a new skill", "improve skill description", "organize skill content", or needs guidance on skill structure, progressive disclosure, or skill development best practices for Claude Code plugins.

skills.name: solo
skills.description: Work on one hard mathematics problem in this session yourself, with no sub-agents: reason in stages, record each settled step in a notes file so that nothing written is lost if a response is cut off, and end with a self-contained proof.md. Usage: /math-proof:solo <the problem, stated in full, or the path of a file holding it>.

skills.name: supplier-escape-to-alternate-source
skills.description: Runs the cross-area chain from a nonconformance traced to purchased material through to an alternate-source RFQ: writes the NCR and its containment, establishes root cause against the supplier rather than the process, records the corrective action, then builds the sourcing package with a response format that makes the returned bids comparable. Use when someone says "run the supplier escape chain," "a supplier caused this, find us an alternate," "supplier escape to alternate source," or asks to source around a supplier who caused a defect.

skills.name: supplier-quote-request
skills.description: Builds the RFQ package that goes out to suppliers — drawing and specification at the verified current revision, the demand picture, the quality clause list, commercial terms, and a mandated response format that makes the returned bids comparable by construction. Lists everything missing. Hard stops on a revision mismatch or restricted technical data. Then runs the supplier loop: candidates from the approved supplier list with unapproved and single-source flagged, one email draft per supplier for the buyer to send, response tracking with chase drafts, returned bids read into one shape with every missing field listed, a comparison per quantity break computed in code, and a recommendation. The buyer decides; the skill records who and when. Use when someone says "source this part," "send an RFQ to suppliers," "we need an alternate supplier," "get quotes on this," "who else can make this?", "chase the suppliers," "compare these bids," or "we're going with this supplier."

skills.name: trade-study-report
skills.description: Turns a filled-in trade study matrix and its analysis results into a scored comparison and a decision memo, with every score cited to its source. Runs the sensitivity analysis every time — where the winner flips, which criterion the decision actually rests on, whether an option never wins under any plausible weighting — because a recommendation with no sensitivity check is a spreadsheet, not a decision. Disqualifies options that violate a hard constraint rather than scoring them low. Consumes design-space-explore's variant manifest when one exists, or a matrix filled in by hand when it doesn't. Use when someone says "compare these options," "write the trade study," "which design should we pick," "score these against the requirements," or "how sensitive is this decision to the weighting."

plugins.name: apollo-graphql-skills
plugins.description: Nine skills for Apollo GraphQL: Client, Server, Router, Federation, Connectors, schema and operation design, and Rust best practices.
plugins.author: Apollo GraphQL
exampleQueries: Design the GraphQL schema for this API
Add federation to these services

skills.name: apollo-client
skills.description: Guide for building React applications with Apollo Client 4.x. Use this skill when: (1) setting up Apollo Client in a React project, (2) writing GraphQL queries or mutations with hooks, (3) configuring caching or cache policies, (4) managing local state with reactive variables, (5) troubleshooting Apollo Client errors or performance issues.

skills.name: apollo-connectors
skills.description: DEPRECATED: superseded by the graphos-factory skill (npx skills add apollographql/skills@graphos-factory), which builds and maintains a Connectors subgraph from a REST API with recorded decisions and verification. Guide for integrating REST APIs into GraphQL supergraphs using Apollo Connectors with @source and @connect directives. Use this skill when the user: (1) mentions "connectors", "Apollo Connectors", or "REST Connector", (2) wants to integrate a REST API into GraphQL, (3) references @source or @connect directives, (4) works with files containing "# Note to AI Friends: This is an Apollo Connectors schema".

skills.name: apollo-federation
skills.description: Guide for authoring Apollo Federation subgraph schemas. Use this skill when: (1) creating new subgraph schemas for a federated supergraph, (2) defining or modifying entities with @key, (3) sharing types/fields across subgraphs with @shareable, (4) working with federation directives (@external, @requires, @provides, @override, @inaccessible), (5) troubleshooting composition errors, (6) any task involving federation schema design patterns.

skills.name: apollo-router
skills.description: Version-aware guide for configuring and running Apollo Router for federated GraphQL supergraphs. Generates correct YAML for both Router v1.x and v2.x. Use this skill when: (1) setting up Apollo Router to run a supergraph, (2) configuring routing, headers, or CORS, (3) implementing custom plugins (Rhai scripts or coprocessors), (4) configuring telemetry (tracing, metrics, logging), (5) troubleshooting Router performance or connectivity issues, (6) securing the graph with JWT, declarative field-level authorization directives, or persisted-query safelisting, (7) managing router.yaml as version-controlled config with CI/CD validation.

skills.name: apollo-router-plugin-creator
skills.description: Guide for writing Apollo Router native Rust plugins. Use this skill when: (1) users want to create a new router plugin, (2) users want to add service hooks (router_service, supergraph_service, execution_service, subgraph_service), (3) users want to modify an existing router plugin, (4) users need to understand router plugin patterns or the request lifecycle. (5) triggers on requests like "create a new plugin", "add a router plugin", "modify the X plugin", or "add subgraph_service hook".

skills.name: apollo-server
skills.description: Guide for building GraphQL servers with Apollo Server 5.x. Use this skill when: (1) setting up a new Apollo Server project, (2) writing resolvers or defining GraphQL schemas, (3) implementing authentication or authorization, (4) creating plugins or custom data sources, (5) troubleshooting Apollo Server errors or performance issues.

skills.name: graphql-operations
skills.description: Guide for writing GraphQL operations (queries, mutations, fragments) following best practices. Use this skill when: (1) writing GraphQL queries or mutations, (2) organizing operations with fragments, (3) optimizing data fetching patterns, (4) setting up type generation or linting, (5) reviewing operations for efficiency.

skills.name: graphql-schema
skills.description: Guide for designing and changing GraphQL schemas following industry best practices. Use this skill whenever you create or edit GraphQL SDL, such as a `schema.graphql` file or `typeDefs`, including when: (1) designing a new GraphQL schema or API, (2) adding or changing types, fields, arguments, mutations, or descriptions in an existing schema, (3) reviewing existing schema for improvements, (4) deciding on type structures or nullability, (5) implementing pagination or error patterns, (6) ensuring security in schema design.

skills.name: rust-best-practices
skills.description: Guide for writing idiomatic Rust code based on Apollo GraphQL's best practices handbook. Use this skill when: (1) writing new Rust code or functions, (2) reviewing or refactoring existing Rust code, (3) deciding between borrowing vs cloning or ownership patterns, (4) implementing error handling with Result types, (5) optimizing Rust code for performance, (6) writing tests or documentation for Rust projects.

skills.name: argent-create-e2e

skills.name: argent-ios-device-setup

skills.name: argent-metro-debugger

Primary path is React Native via Metro (iOS / Android / Vega); a subset of the tools (debugger-connect, debugger-status, debugger-evaluate, debugger-log-registry) also drive a Chromium (CDP) app's renderer (an Electron app, or any Chromium browser exposing CDP) through the same surface. Use when connecting to the runtime, inspecting React components, reading console logs, or evaluating JavaScript.

skills.name: argent-native-profiler
skills.description: Diagnose native CPU hotspots, UI hangs, and memory issues. Use Instruments (xctrace) on iOS simulators and Mac apps, or Perfetto on Android. Use when diagnosing native-level performance issues.

skills.name: argent-qa-e2e
skills.description: Write repeatable QA regression e2e tests from test cases, tickets, or acceptance criteria. Use when the user asks to write, automate, or generate an e2e test or preserve an automated regression scenario, with deterministic setup, stable targets, executable structural or visual evidence, and two consecutive full passes. For one-off UI checks or replayable paths without acceptance criteria, use argent-test-ui-flow or argent-create-e2e. skills.name: argent-react-native-app-workflow

skills.name: argent-react-native-optimization
skills.description: Optimizes a React Native app by profiling first to find real bottlenecks, then sweeping for mechanical issues. Entry-point for all performance work. Use when the app feels slow, user asks to optimize, fix re-renders, reduce jank, or improve startup. Delegates to argent-react-native-profiler for measurement.

skills.name: argent-react-native-profiler
skills.description: Profile a React Native Hermes app to measure re-render and CPU performance using argent profiler tools. Use when optimizing for performance, measuring before/after a fix, spotting slow components, diagnosing re-renders, checking CPU hotspots, or producing a ranked issue report.

skills.name: argent-screen-recording
skills.description: Record a video of an iOS simulator or Android emulator/device screen using argent MCP tools. Use when the user asks to record the screen, capture a video of a flow, interaction, or animation, produce a screen recording, or document app behavior as a video clip.

skills.name: argent-screenshot-diff
skills.description: Compare saved or live app screenshots with the argent screenshot-diff tool. Use when testing visual regressions, before/after UI comparisons, screenshot diff checks, visible layout, spacing, color, typography, clipping, overflow, text rendering, or image/icon rendering changes.

skills.name: argent-settings-permissions
skills.description: Grant, deny, or reset an app's runtime permissions (camera, microphone, photos, contacts, notifications, calendar, location, location-always, media-library, motion, reminders) on an iOS simulator or Android device using the argent `settings-permissions` tool - without navigating the system Settings UI. Use when the permission cannot be changed through the app itself - and only then, pre-authorize before the app asks, deny up front, re-enable a permission the user already denied, or reset so the prompt reappears. If the app can flip it - via an in-app toggle or the system permission dialog the app triggers - interact with the app instead.

skills.name: argent-test-ui-flow
skills.description: Autonomously test an app UI (iOS or Android) by running interact-screenshot-verify loops using argent MCP tools. Use when testing UI flows, verifying login works, testing navigation, running UI test scenarios, manual QA steps, visible UI changes, or visual behavior.

skills.name: argent-tv-interact
skills.description: Control and inspect TV apps via argent, Apple TV (tvOS), Android TV (leanback), and Amazon Fire TV (Vega). Use when a task targets a TV (runtimeKind "tv", or platform "vega"), or mentions Apple TV / tvOS / Android TV / leanback / Vega / Fire TV / VVD.

plugins.description: Seventeen skills for spec-driven development: writing the spec, the design and the tasks, and letting an agent work from them.
plugins.author: gotalab
exampleQueries: Write a spec for this feature
Break this spec into tasks

skills.name: kiro-debug
skills.description: Investigate implementation failures using root-cause-first debugging. Use when an implementer is blocked, verification fails, or repeated remediation does not converge.

skills.name: kiro-discovery
skills.description: Entry point for new work. Determines the best action path or work decomposition (update existing spec, create new spec, mixed decomposition, or no spec needed) and refines ideas through structured dialogue.

skills.name: kiro-impl
skills.description: Implement approved tasks using TDD with subagent dispatch. Runs all pending tasks autonomously or selected tasks manually.

skills.name: kiro-review
skills.description: Review a task implementation against approved specs, task boundaries, and verification evidence. Use after an implementer finishes a task, after remediation, or before accepting a task as complete.

skills.name: kiro-spec-batch
skills.description: Create complete specs (requirements, design, tasks) for all features in roadmap.md using parallel sub-agent dispatch by dependency wave.

skills.name: kiro-spec-design
skills.description: Create comprehensive technical design for a specification

skills.name: kiro-spec-init
skills.description: Initialize a new specification with detailed project description

skills.name: kiro-spec-quick
skills.description: Quick spec generation with interactive or automatic mode

skills.name: kiro-spec-requirements
skills.description: Generate comprehensive requirements for a specification

skills.name: kiro-spec-status
skills.description: Show specification status and progress

skills.name: kiro-spec-tasks
skills.description: Generate implementation tasks for a specification

skills.name: kiro-steering
skills.description: Manage {{KIRO_DIR}}/steering/ as persistent project knowledge

skills.name: kiro-steering-custom
skills.description: Create custom steering documents for specialized project contexts

skills.name: kiro-validate-design
skills.description: Interactive technical design quality review and validation

skills.name: kiro-validate-gap
skills.description: Analyze implementation gap between requirements and existing codebase

This session is getting long — what should I drop?

skills.name: bdi-mental-states
skills.description: This skill should be used when modeling agent mental states with BDI concepts: beliefs, desires, intentions, RDF-to-belief transformations, rational agency traces, cognitive agents, BDI ontologies, and neuro-symbolic AI integration.

skills.name: latent-briefing
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user asks to "share memory between agents", "KV cache compaction for multi-agent", "orchestrator worker context", "latent briefing", "reduce worker tokens", "cross-agent memory without summarization", or discusses Attention Matching compaction, recursive language models with workers, or token explosion in hierarchical agents.

skills.name: long-horizon-prompting
skills.description: This skill should be used when writing, enhancing, or evaluating the launch prompt for a long-running autonomous agent or a parallel multi-agent orchestration attacking a hard problem: pseudo-formal task briefs that define terms and an exact success predicate linguistically, enumerate non-counting outcomes, set persistence rules with explicit stop and return conditions and effort floors, manage a diverse portfolio of parallel approaches with an approach registry and blocked-route bookkeeping, and gate the return on adversarial audit. Route agent topology and coordination protocols to multi-agent-patterns, runtime control surfaces and loop governance to harness-engineering, evaluator and quality-gate construction to evaluation, judge design to advanced-evaluation, and compaction or memory mechanics to context-compression and memory-systems.

skills.name: self-improvement-loops
skills.description: This skill should be used when the harness, scaffold, workflow, or optimizer itself is the optimization target: recursive self-improvement (RSI) loops, meta-harnesses, self-improving harnesses that mine their own failures and propose bounded edits, evolutionary or population-based search over agent scaffolds, acceptance gates for self-modifying systems, and agentic context evolution where the mechanism that produces context is versioned and evolved. Route governance of a single autonomous loop (locked surfaces, durable logs, rollback, novelty gates, approval boundaries) to harness-engineering, measurement and quality-gate design to evaluation, judge design to advanced-evaluation, and remote sandbox infrastructure to hosted-agents.

skills.name: self-managed-context
skills.description: This skill should be used when a model gets read-write control over its own live context window instead of a harness-scheduled compaction policy: the context exposed as an editable file the model rewrites with code tools, model-driven eviction and in-place updates, the harness invariants that keep self-editing safe (pinned prefix, edit gate, edit receipts, budget readouts, rollback on overflow), the prefix-cache cost of mid-context edits, and steering or training the model's own context-editing strategy. Route note content and fixed-threshold summarization to context-compression, cache-stable layout under harness control to context-optimization, file offloading to filesystem-context, and loop governance to self-improvement-loops.

skills.name: docker-agent-config
skills.description: Use this skill when creating or editing an agent.yaml (or .yml/.hcl) configuration file for Docker Agent (cagent), including defining agents, models/providers, built-in or MCP toolsets, multi-agent teams with sub_agents. Even if the user just says they want to "build an AI agent with Docker", "make a coding agent config", "add a tool to my agent", or "set up a team of agents", this skill applies. Covers agent properties (model, instruction, toolsets, sub_agents, fallback), the models/providers sections, built-in toolsets (filesystem, shell, think, todo, memory, fetch), MCP toolset references, and named commands.

Even if the user just says they want to "turn my agent into an MCP server", "let Claude Desktop use my agent", "publish my agent to Docker Hub", "push my agent like an image", or "test my agent in CI", this skill applies. Covers `serve mcp/api/a2a/acp/chat` listen addresses and auth flags, `share push/pull`, eval session JSON format, scoring metrics, and the `--baseline` regression gate.

skills.name: docker-agent-run
skills.description: Use this skill when running a Docker Agent with `docker agent run`, choosing a safety/approval mode, using the `--sandbox` isolation flag, setting up aliases, or troubleshooting a run (missing credentials, worktrees). Even if the user just says they want to "run my agent", "make my agent auto-approve tool calls", "run this agent safely", or "why can't my agent see my API key", this skill applies. Covers `--safety` (strict/balanced/restricted/autonomous), `--yolo`, `--sandbox` and its network allowlist, `--worktree`, `docker agent alias`, and `docker agent doctor`.

skills.name: docker-destructive-guardrails
skills.description: Use this skill before running, or recommending, any Docker command that deletes, wipes, resets, or otherwise irreversibly changes state — even if the user just says to "clean up", "clear the cache", "start fresh", "wipe everything", "nuke it", "reset", "force remove", or "tear down" Docker resources. Covers generic Docker CLI destructive operations not owned by a more specific skill — `docker rm`, `docker rm -f`, `docker container prune`, `docker kill`, `docker system prune`, `docker rmi`/`docker image rm`, `docker image prune -a`, `docker network rm`, `docker network prune`, `docker builder prune`, `docker buildx rm`, `docker context rm`, and standalone (non-Compose) `docker volume rm`/`docker volume prune`. Also indexes destructive commands owned by other Docker skills (Compose, sandbox, Desktop). Core rule — state exactly what will be lost and get explicit confirmation first, except narrow, low-friction Tier 1 container cleanup.

skills.name: docker-docs
skills.description: Use this skill to answer questions about any Docker product from current official Docker documentation instead of memory, even if the user just asks "how do I…", "does Docker support…", "what's the flag for…", or "is this still the right way" about Docker. Covers Docker Desktop, Engine, Build/Buildx/Build Cloud, Compose, Hub, Scout, Docker Hardened Images (DHI), Offload, Testcontainers, Docker Sandboxes (`sbx`, local and cloud sandboxes, Sandboxes API/SDK), Docker Agentic Platform, Docker Agent, MCP Catalog/Toolkit/Gateway, Model Runner, Gordon, and account, admin, security, and billing docs. skills.name: docker-sandboxes-lifecycle

Covers `sbx run`/`sbx create` (including the built-in agents claude, codex, cursor, devin, docker-agent, gemini, opencode, shell), workspace bind-mount vs `--clone` isolation, additional read-only workspaces, reattaching by `--name`, `sbx ls`/`stop`/`rm`/`prune`, `sbx exec`, `sbx cp`, and `sbx ports`.

skills.name: docker-sandboxes-network-credentials

skills.description: Guides agents in compiling and packaging C/C++ source code into dynamic or static libraries (Code Assets) using Dart's Native Assets hook system (via hook/build.dart and hook/link.dart utilizing package:hooks and package:native_toolchain_c). Use when a user asks to: 'setup native assets', 'compile C/C++ source code', 'bundle dynamic libraries', 'build native C code', 'link native assets', 'implement build.dart or link.dart hooks', or 'integrate C/C++ interop in Dart/Flutter'. Helps agents avoid manual toolchain orchestration and configures secure hash-validated binary downloads or advanced linker tree-shaking with package:record_use mapping.

skills.name: dart-use-doc-examples
skills.description: How to inject external code examples into Dartdoc using the {@example} directive, and how to filter those files using #hide, #region, and #endregion tags.

skills.name: dart-use-ffigen
skills.description: Guide agents to use `package:ffigen` to automatically generate FFI bindings instead of writing them manually. Use this skill when a task involves writing new FFI bindings, extending C/Objective-C/Swift integrations, or replacing hand-crafted `dart:ffi` setups.

skills.name: dart-use-primary-constructors
skills.description: Help users write syntactically and semantically correct primary constructors in Dart, and migrate/use the new constructor syntax, empty-body semicolon syntax, in-body initializer list syntax, and abbreviated concise constructor syntax.

skills.name: dart-write-documentation
skills.description: Rules and formatting guidelines for writing Dart /// API documentation and doc comments. Use when documenting Dart code, writing doc comments for any Dart declaration (libraries, classes, methods, variables, etc.), or when instructed to follow the Effective Dart documentation guidelines.

skills.name: flutter-add-integration-test
skills.description: Configures Flutter Driver for app interaction and converts MCP actions into permanent integration tests. Use when adding integration testing to a project, exploring UI components via MCP, or automating user flows with the integration_test package.

skills.name: flutter-add-widget-preview
skills.description: Adds interactive widget previews to the project using the previews.dart system. Use when creating new UI components or updating existing screens to ensure consistent design and interactive testing.

skills.name: flutter-add-widget-test
skills.description: Implement a component-level test using `WidgetTester` to verify UI rendering and user interactions (tapping, scrolling, entering text). Use when validating that a specific widget displays correct data and responds to events as expected.

skills.name: flutter-apply-architecture-best-practices
skills.description: Architects a Flutter application using the recommended layered approach (UI, Logic, Data). Use when structuring a new project or refactoring for scalability.

skills.name: flutter-build-responsive-layout
skills.description: Use `LayoutBuilder`, `MediaQuery`, or `Expanded/Flexible` to create a layout that adapts to different screen sizes. Use when you need the UI to look good on both mobile and tablet/desktop form factors.

skills.name: flutter-fix-layout-issues
skills.description: Fixes Flutter layout errors (overflows, unbounded constraints) using Dart and Flutter MCP tools. Use when addressing "RenderFlex overflowed", "Vertical viewport was given unbounded height", or similar layout issues.

skills.name: flutter-implement-json-serialization
skills.description: Create model classes with `fromJson` and `toJson` methods using `dart:convert`. Use when manually mapping JSON keys to class properties for simple data structures.

skills.name: flutter-setup-declarative-routing
skills.description: Configure `MaterialApp.router` using a package like `go_router` for advanced URL-based navigation. Use when developing web applications or mobile apps that require specific deep linking and browser history support.

skills.name: flutter-setup-localization
skills.description: Add `flutter_localizations` and `intl` dependencies, enable "generate true" in `pubspec.yaml`, and create an `l10n.yaml` configuration file. Use when initializing localization support for a new Flutter project.

skills.name: flutter-use-http-package
skills.description: Use the `http` package to execute GET, POST, PUT, or DELETE requests. Use when you need to fetch from or send data to a REST API.

plugins.name: frontend-craft-skills
plugins.description: Fourteen skills for interface craft: animation vocabulary and performance, reviewing animations, gestures, Apple-style design, native mobile and Swift work, picking a UI library and learning taste.
plugins.author: Emil Kowalski
exampleQueries: Review this animation for performance
Add a gesture to this screen
Which UI library fits this app?

skills.name: animate
skills.description: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.

skills.name: animate-expo
skills.description: Build animations in React Native and Expo, making the decisions in the order that determines whether they feel right — should it animate, which thread it runs on, which properties, spring or timing, how the gesture hands off, how it degrades. Writes the implementation with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and expo-haptics. Use when animating anything in an Expo app, adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions, press feedback or haptics, or fixing motion that stutters on device. For web animation use `animate`.

skills.name: animation-performance
skills.description: Keep web animations inside the frame budget — animate composite-only properties, keep motion off the main thread when the page is busy, and find the cause when an animation drops frames. Use when an animation is janky, choppy, stutters, or drops frames; when choosing which property to animate; when deciding between CSS and JS animation on performance grounds; or when reaching for `will-change` or GPU layers. For choosing easing, duration, or whether to animate at all use animate; for reviewing motion as a whole use review-animations.

skills.name: animation-vocabulary
skills.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.

skills.name: apple-design
skills.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

skills.name: ask-emil
skills.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

skills.name: ask-sonner
skills.description: Guide to Sonner, the React toast library — install and wire up the Toaster, pick the right toast() call, promise and loading toasts, updating, dismissing and persisting toasts, styling, theming and icons, positioning and multiple toasters. Use when working with Sonner or troubleshooting it — toasts that don't appear, appear twice, lose their styles, ignore Tailwind classes, sit behind a modal, or don't follow dark mode.

skills.name: emil-design-eng
skills.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great. Use when building or reviewing a UI component's interactions and polish (press and hover states, popover origin, tooltip timing, transitions vs keyframes, clip-path techniques, drag details) and no narrower skill fits.

skills.name: gestures
skills.description: Build drag, swipe, and sheet interactions that track the finger 1:1 and stay interruptible. Use when building or fixing anything the user drags, swipes, flings, holds, or dismisses with a gesture — drawers, sheets, swipe-to-dismiss toasts and cards, drag-to-reorder, pull-to-refresh, hold-to-confirm — or when a gesture feels laggy, disconnected from the finger, jumps on release, or can't be caught mid-animation. Triggers on — gesture, drag, swipe, fling, sheet, snap points, Vaul, Motion drag props, rubber-band, pull to refresh, hold to delete, touch-action, "doesn't follow my finger", "jumps when I let go", "can't grab it mid-animation".

skills.name: learn-taste
skills.description: Turn a session's design corrections into rules, with their why, in DESIGN.md, a project skill, or a lint check.

skills.name: mobile-native
skills.description: Make a web app feel native on a phone — the small CSS and meta-tag fixes that separate "a website in a browser" from something that feels installed. Covers sticky hover states, tap highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom the page, laggy taps, pull-to-refresh hijacking scroll, content under the notch, long-press selecting button text, carousels that scroll the wrong way, mismatched status bars, and the rule that you test on real hardware. Use when a web app is being built for or reviewed on mobile, when something "works in Chrome but feels wrong on my phone", when building a PWA, a bottom sheet, a carousel, a full-screen layout, or any touch interaction. For motion itself use animate; for React Native use animate-expo.

skills.name: pick-ui-library
skills.description: Pick the library for a frontend task from a curated list — primitives, toasts, drawers, command menus, OTP, numbers, charts, virtualization, drag and drop, state, styling.

skills.name: review-animations
skills.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

skills.name: write-swift
skills.description: How to write modern Swift well — modeling with value types, Swift 6 data-race safety and approachable concurrency (@concurrent, main-actor-by-default, actors, task groups), protocols and generics (some vs any), API design, performance and ARC, Swift Testing, macros, and the modern language features agents don't know about yet. Use when writing, reviewing, or migrating Swift, or when a concurrency error, a hang, a data race, a retain cycle, or a performance problem needs fixing.

plugins.name: game-development-skills
plugins.description: Sixty-three skills for game development: AI behaviour trees and utility AI, camera systems, audio, dialogue, card games, FPS and Bevy ECS.
plugins.author: gamedev-skills
exampleQueries: Write the behaviour tree for this enemy
Set up the camera in this game
How do I structure this Bevy ECS?

skills.name: ai-behavior-trees-utility-ai
skills.description: Engine-neutral behavior tree and utility AI code for NPCs in any language: Blackboard, reactive composites, decorators and response-curve scoring. Use when an enemy keeps chasing after losing sight, restarts its action every frame or flip-flops between choices. Not for FSMs, steering or pathfinding (`game-ai`) or Unreal BT, EQS and StateTree (`unreal-behavior-trees`).

skills.name: audio-design
skills.description: Engine-neutral game audio technique: bus layout, volume sliders in decibels, loudness, ducking music under dialogue, adaptive music and SFX variation, with Godot, Unity and FMOD/Wwise mappings. Use when mixing a game, making music react to combat, fixing repetitive footsteps or beat sync, or a mix that clips or pumps. Not for the Godot audio API (`godot-audio`).

skills.name: bevy-ecs
skills.description: Builds and debugs Bevy 0.20 games in Rust: components, Query and Commands systems, schedules, States, observers and headless tests. Use when Cargo.toml depends on bevy, on a B0001 query-conflict panic, or pre-0.20 code (EventReader, SpriteBundle). Not for engine-neutral AI, generation, physics or shaders (`game-ai`, `procedural-gen`, `physics-tuning`, `shader-programming`).

skills.name: camera-systems
skills.description: Builds and tunes game cameras, engine-neutral with Godot and Cinemachine 3 mappings: 2D follow with deadzone and look-ahead, third-person orbit, first-person look and split-screen. Use when the camera lags, jitters while following, shows past the level edge, clips through walls or changes with frame rate. Not for shake (`game-feel`) or physics timestep jitter (`physics-tuning`).

skills.name: card-game
skills.description: Designs card games and deckbuilders in any engine: cards as data with one effect interpreter, deck zones, a trigger stack and seeded shuffles. Use for a Slay the Spire- or Balatro-like or a TCG, or cards that duplicate or streaky shuffles. Pair with the engine skill for card data and hand UI (`godot-resources`, `godot-ui-control`, `unity-scriptableobjects`). Not for grid crawlers (`roguelike`).

skills.name: dialogue-systems
skills.description: Builds engine-neutral branching dialogue with Ink, Yarn Spinner or a small JSON graph runner: lines, choices, conditions, variables and localization IDs. Use for NPC conversations, dialogue trees, barks, .ink or .yarn files, or dialogue that dead-ends. Not for visual-novel backlog and skip (`visual-novel`), quests (`rpg`) or text box widgets (`godot-ui-control`, `game-ui-ux`).

skills.name: fps-shooter
skills.description: Designs first-person shooter combat in any engine: hitscan vs projectiles, time-to-kill, damage falloff, recoil patterns, ADS sensitivity and lag-compensated hits. Use for a Doom- or Counter-Strike-like, or guns that feel weak or shots that do not register. Not for the camera rig (`camera-systems`), shake and hit-stop (`game-feel`) or raycast APIs (`godot-physics`, `unity-physics`).

skills.name: game-ai
skills.description: Designs engine-neutral enemy and NPC AI: picks FSM, behavior tree, utility or GOAP, and builds perception, steering and A* pathfinding. Use for patrol and chase, "find a path to the player", agents stuck on corners or AI that sees through walls. Not for BT or utility code (`ai-behavior-trees-utility-ai`), Unreal AI (`unreal-behavior-trees`) or Unity NavMesh (`unity-navmesh`).

skills.name: game-feel
skills.description: Adds engine-neutral juice to a working mechanic: trauma-based screen shake, hit-stop, eased tweens, squash and stretch, and knockback. Use when the game feels flat, weightless or not punchy, or hits and jumps should feel satisfying. Not for coyote time (`platformer`), input buffering (`input-systems`), camera follow (`camera-systems`) or HUD layout (`game-ui-ux`).

skills.name: game-jam
skills.description: Plans and ships a game jam entry against a fixed deadline: reads the jam rules, scopes to the clock, keeps a cut list and checks the build before submitting. Use for Ludum Dare, GMTK, Global Game Jam or any itch.io jam, a 48-hour game, or "we're behind, what do we cut". Not for untimed experiments (`prototype-fast`) or upload commands (`itch-publish`).

skills.name: game-ui-ux
skills.description: Engine-neutral design rules for game HUDs and menus: anchors and containers, scaling, safe areas, gamepad focus, HUDs driven by events instead of polling, and accessibility minimums. Use for menus, health bars or inventory screens that break on ultrawide or phones. Pair with `godot-ui-control` or `roblox-ui`. Not for button juice (`game-feel`) or rebinding (`input-systems`).

skills.name: godot-csharp
skills.description: C# and .NET in Godot 4.7: partial node classes, the PascalCase lifecycle, [Export] and [Signal], signals as C# events, the .csproj and calling GDScript. Use for .cs scripts in Godot, porting GDScript to C#, a failed build, or a failed web or Android export. Not for GDScript (`godot-gdscript`), Unity C# (`unity-csharp-scripting`) or export presets (`godot-export`).

skills.name: godot-export
skills.description: Exports Godot 4.7 projects: templates, export_presets.cfg for desktop, Web and Android, command-line exports and web COOP/COEP headers. Use on "No export template found", a blank web build, a SharedArrayBuffer error or files missing after export. Not for tests in CI (`godot-gdscript-headless-testing`), store uploads (`steam-publish`, `itch-publish`) or netcode (`godot-multiplayer`).

skills.name: godot-gdscript-headless-testing
skills.description: Runs Godot 4.7 GDScript tests with godot --headless and a SceneTree runner that exits non-zero on failure, so CI can gate merges. Owns Godot tests in CI. Use for GitHub Actions jobs or a headless run that hangs or exits 0 despite SCRIPT ERROR lines. Not for export in CI (`godot-export`), GDScript language (`godot-gdscript`) or Unity tests (`unity-csharp-scripting`).

skills.name: godot-multiplayer
skills.description: Godot 4.7 high-level multiplayer: ENet host and join, @rpc with rpc_id(), MultiplayerSpawner and MultiplayerSynchronizer, with a two-instance headless test. Use for online or LAN co-op in Godot, or a rejected RPC, spawned nodes missing on clients, or state that does not sync. Not for Roblox (`roblox-networking`), server exports (`godot-export`) or local split-screen (`camera-systems`).

skills.name: godot-physics
skills.description: Godot 4.7 physics API in 2D and 3D: body and Area types, collision_layer and mask bits, Area signals for hurtboxes, RayCast and space queries, and Jolt (3D default since 4.6). Use when objects pass through each other, body_entered never fires or a raycast hits itself. Not for engine-neutral jitter and tunnelling (`physics-tuning`) or CharacterBody movement (`godot-2d-movement`).

skills.name: godot-resources
skills.description: Godot 4.7 data-driven design with custom Resources: class_name and @export fields, .tres files, shared references vs duplicate_deep(), uids and threaded loading. Use for items, stats or enemy configs as data, or when editing one enemy changes every enemy or a .tres stops loading. Not for save slots (`save-systems`) or the C# version (`godot-csharp`).

skills.name: godot-shaders
skills.description: Godot 4.7 Shading Language syntax and pipeline: canvas_item, spatial and particle shaders, built-ins, ShaderMaterial wiring, a headless compile check and 3.x porting. Use for a .gdshader, a SHADER ERROR, shader parameters set from GDScript, or an effect that looks washed out or sorts wrong. Not for effect maths such as dissolve or outline (`shader-programming`).

skills.name: godot-signals-groups
skills.description: Godot 4.7 signals and node groups: typed signals, connect() with Callables, one-shot and deferred connections, event-bus autoloads and call_group broadcasts. Use when nodes must talk without hard references, a handler fires twice or never, or the log says "already connected". Not for GDScript syntax (`godot-gdscript`) or autoload setup (`godot-nodes-scenes`).

skills.name: godot-tilemap
skills.description: Godot 4.7 tile maps with TileMapLayer and TileSet: atlas sources, data layers, terrain autotiling and set_cell or local_to_map at runtime. Use for 2D tile levels in Godot, tiles with no collision, a click on the wrong cell or porting a deprecated TileMap. Not for Unity (`unity-tilemap-2d`), tile art (`create-game-assets`) or generation (`procedural-gen`).

skills.name: godot-ui-control
skills.description: Godot 4.7 Control-node API for menus and HUDs: anchors, Containers, Theme and StyleBox, focus neighbours and stretch settings, with a headless layout check. Use when Godot UI overlaps or drifts on resize, buttons ignore the gamepad, or an invisible panel swallows clicks. Not for engine-neutral UI rules (`game-ui-ux`; load both) or rebinding (`input-systems`).

skills.name: input-systems
skills.description: Engine-neutral input architecture with Godot InputMap code: named actions, stick deadzones, buffered presses and rebinding with conflict checks. Use for controller support or a rebind menu, or a drifting stick, WASD on AZERTY, or a dropped press. Not for coyote time (`platformer`) or Unity and Unreal input assets (`unity-input-system`, `unreal-enhanced-input`).

skills.name: itch-publish
skills.description: Publishes and updates games on itch.io with the butler CLI: butler push to user/game:channel, channel platform tags, HTML5 builds, --userversion and CI uploads. Use for "upload to itch", an HTML5 game that downloads instead of playing, a blank or 403 web build, or "invalid target". Not for Steam (`steam-publish`) or jam scope (`game-jam`).

skills.name: level-design
skills.description: Engine-neutral level design with Godot checks: player metrics from the real controller, key and ability gating with a soft-lock check, and pacing. Use when laying out a level or metroidvania gates, or players get lost or a key sits behind its own door. Not for generation (`procedural-gen`), painting tiles (`godot-tilemap`, `unity-tilemap-2d`) or jump tuning (`platformer`).

skills.name: love2d-core
skills.description: Builds and debugs LÖVE (Love2D) 11.x games in Lua: main.lua callbacks, conf.lua, fixed steps, crisp pixel-art scaling, love.filesystem saves and a scripted run. Use when main.lua calls love.*, or on blurry pixel art, the blue error screen or speed tied to frame rate. Not for Defold (`defold-core`) or engine-neutral saves and input (`save-systems`, `input-systems`).

skills.name: phaser-arcade-physics
skills.description: Phaser 4 Arcade Physics movement and collision: bodies, velocity, gravity, colliders vs overlaps, groups and bullet pools. Use for a Phaser platformer or top-down controller, or a sprite that ignores physics, onFloor() always false or bodies passing through walls. Not for scenes and the loader (`phaser-core`), coyote time (`platformer`) or tunnelling theory (`physics-tuning`).

skills.name: phaser-core
skills.description: Sets up and debugs Phaser 4 games (and pinned Phaser 3.90): Game config, Scene lifecycle, the loader, scene transitions and Phaser 3 to 4 migration. Use when code imports phaser, or on a black screen, assets undefined in create, or a HUD scene behind the game. Not for colliders (`phaser-arcade-physics`), HUD layout (`game-ui-ux`) or PixiJS (`pixijs-rendering`).

skills.name: physics-tuning
skills.description: Engine-neutral physics tuning with Godot checks: fixed timestep and interpolation, CCD against tunnelling, damping, solver iterations and collision layer matrices. Use when bodies jitter, fast objects pass through walls or physics feels floaty or wrong. Not for engine physics APIs (`godot-physics`, `unity-physics`, `roblox-physics`, `phaser-arcade-physics`) or jump feel (`platformer`).

skills.name: pixijs-rendering
skills.description: Builds and debugs 2D browser game rendering with PixiJS v8: async init, Assets loading, the Container and Sprite scene graph, pointer dragging and v7-to-v8 migration. Use when a game or playable ad uses pixi.js, or on a blank canvas, clicks not firing, or drag stopping at the sprite edge. Not for dashboards or charts, Phaser (`phaser-core`) or 3D (`threejs-scene-setup`).

skills.name: procedural-gen
skills.description: Engine-neutral procedural generation in Python with Godot and Unity mappings: seeded RNG, dungeon layouts, wave function collapse, noise terrain and loot tables. Use for a dungeon generator, WFC or Perlin terrain, or seeds that give different maps. Not for roguelike run structure (`roguelike`), deckbuilders (`card-game`) or painting tiles (`godot-tilemap`, `unity-tilemap-2d`).

skills.name: prototype-fast
skills.description: Builds a throwaway playable prototype in about an hour to answer one question, usually "is this mechanic fun?": a one-question brief, a greybox, a debug HUD, a playtest and a keep, kill or retune call. Use for "prototype this", "just get something playable" or whether to keep prototype code. Not for a timed jam (`game-jam`) or level blockouts (`level-design`).

skills.name: puzzle
skills.description: Designs grid and logic puzzle games in any engine: match-3 cascades, Sokoban pushing, unique-solution grids (nonogram, Sudoku), exact undo and solver-checked levels. Use for a Candy Crush-like, Sokoban or Picross, or broken cascades, drifting undo or unsolvable levels. Not for physics puzzlers (`platformer`, `physics-tuning`) or card games (`card-game`).

skills.name: pygame-core
skills.description: Builds and debugs 2D games in Python with pygame-ce (imported as pygame): the event-update-draw loop, delta time, Surfaces and Rects, Sprite groups and headless tests. Use when code imports pygame, or a window says not responding, speed differs per PC or pygame and pygame-ce conflict. Not for engine-neutral input or saves (`input-systems`, `save-systems`) or jump feel (`platformer`).

skills.name: roblox-characters
skills.description: Roblox player characters: CharacterAdded lifecycle, Humanoid and HumanoidRootPart, R6, R15 and custom rigs, respawn and Tools. Use when a character script breaks after respawn, animations do not play or replicate, or sprint code fights the Humanoid. Not for hit validation (`roblox-networking`), forces and raycasts (`roblox-physics`) or cameras (`camera-systems`).

skills.name: roblox-datastores
skills.description: Roblox DataStoreService persistence: load on join, save on leave and BindToClose, UpdateAsync vs SetAsync, session locking and OrderedDataStore leaderboards. Use for lost player data, items duplicating after teleport, or "too many requests" errors. Not for engine-neutral saves (`save-systems`), Luau basics (`roblox-luau`) or economy numbers (`roblox-simulator-economy`).

skills.name: roblox-luau
skills.description: Roblox Luau scripting and code structure: services, Instances, Script vs LocalScript vs ModuleScript, the task library and typed Luau, with selene and luau-lsp checks. Use when a LocalScript does not run, a client gets nil after joining or wait() needs replacing. Not for remotes (`roblox-networking`), saving (`roblox-datastores`) or live-place edits (`roblox-studio-workflow`).

skills.name: roblox-networking
skills.description: Roblox client-server networking and anti-exploit: RemoteEvent and RemoteFunction contracts, server authority, rate limits, hit validation and replication. Use when a remote trusts the client, exploiters spam remotes or gain items, or hits register wrongly. Not for Luau basics (`roblox-luau`), saving (`roblox-datastores`) or force and raycast APIs (`roblox-physics`).

skills.name: roblox-physics
skills.description: Roblox physics and spatial queries: assemblies, constraints, collision groups, Raycast and Shapecast, and network ownership. Use when parts fall through or jitter, Touched is unreliable, a ray hits the shooter, or BodyMovers need replacing. Not for hit legitimacy (`roblox-networking`), Humanoid movement (`roblox-characters`) or engine-neutral tuning (`physics-tuning`).

skills.name: roblox-studio-workflow
skills.description: Safely edits an existing Roblox place or Rojo project: finds the source of truth and proves changes with the right test mode or Studio MCP (execute_luau). Use when an agent edits a .rbxl or Rojo project, works through Studio MCP tools, or must report what was tested. Not for installing Studio MCP (`roblox-get-started`) or the feature code (`roblox-luau`, `roblox-ui`).

skills.name: roblox-ui
skills.description: Roblox UI with ScreenGui and PlayerGui: ResetOnSpawn, UDim2 scale and offset, UIListLayout flex, safe areas, StyleSheet, gamepad selection and touch controls. Use for Roblox HUDs, shops or settings menus, or UI that clips on phones, resets on respawn or loses controller focus. Load `game-ui-ux` too. Not for input mapping (`input-systems`) or purchase checks (`roblox-networking`).

skills.name: roguelike
skills.description: Designs run-based roguelikes and roguelites in any engine: run structure, permadeath, meta-progression, seeded and daily runs, turn order and symmetric field of view. Use for NetHack- or Hades-style games, or runs that feel cheap. Pair with `procedural-gen` for dungeon generation and `save-systems` for run vs meta saves. Not for roguelike deckbuilders (`card-game`).

skills.name: router
skills.description: Routes any game-development request to the right skills: detects the engine (Godot, Unity, Unreal, Ebitengine, Bevy, Phaser, PixiJS, three.js, Defold, LÖVE, pygame, Roblox) and the task, then reads the chosen skill. Use to make a game or when unsure which gamedev skill fits a gameplay, art, UI, audio, AI, genre or shipping task.

skills.name: rpg
skills.description: Designs RPG progression and combat numbers in any engine: stats with a modifier stack, XP curves, damage formulas, items and equipment (slots, rarity, affixes) and quests. Use for a JRPG or Diablo-style looter, or stats wrong after unequipping. Pair with `save-systems` to save characters and inventory. Not for crafting and carry weight (`survival-crafting`) or dialogue (`dialogue-systems`).

skills.name: save-systems
skills.description: Engine-neutral save and load with Godot and Python code: what to serialize, slots and autosave, atomic writes and versioned migration. Use for save/load or a continue button, or saves that corrupt after a crash or break after a patch. plugins.name: google-adk-skills
plugins.description: Eight skills for the Agent Development Kit: building agents and tools, sessions and state, and running them locally or deployed.
plugins.author: Google
exampleQueries: Build an agent with the ADK
Add a tool to this ADK agent

skills.name: adk-agent-builder
skills.description: Builds ADK (Agent Development Kit) Python agents: LLM agents with tools, graph workflows of function and agent nodes, conditional routing, fan-out and join, schema-validated delegation between agents, human-in-the-loop pauses, and pytest coverage for all of it. Use when asked to create an agent or a workflow, add a tool to one, branch or loop between nodes, run steps in parallel, pause for user approval, or test an agent. Don't use for explaining how ADK works internally or designing its core components (use `adk-architecture`), for an agent that already runs but misbehaves (use `adk-debug`), for authoring a sample under `contributing/` (use `adk-sample-creator`), or for naming, typing, and formatting conventions (use `adk-style`).

skills.name: adk-architecture
skills.description: Explains how the ADK runtime fits together: the node and graph execution model, Context and Event flow, checkpoint and resume, tracing, and the rules governing the public API surface. Use when answering "how does X work" about ADK internals, tracing where an event or a piece of state comes from, deciding where a new capability belongs, reviewing a change to BaseNode, Workflow, Runner, Agent, Event or Context, working out why a node re-ran or stayed waiting after a resume, or judging whether a change breaks the public API. Don't use for assembling an agent from existing pieces (use adk-agent-builder), diagnosing one failing run or test (use adk-debug), or formatting and naming conventions (use adk-style).

skills.name: adk-debug
skills.description: Diagnoses misbehaving ADK agents by inspecting sessions, events, tool calls, and the exact request that reached the model. Covers the `adk run` CLI and the `adk web` dev server with its session, trace, and debug HTTP endpoints. Use when an agent returns the wrong answer, ignores a tool or swallows a tool error, hangs, loops, emits raw JSON instead of calling tools, is not discovered by `adk web`, when a sub-agent cannot see the parent conversation, or when you need the LLM request/response, token counts, or logs for a run. Don't use for how ADK is designed internally (use `adk-architecture`), for building a new agent or workflow (use `adk-agent-builder`), for environment or dependency setup failures (use `adk-setup`), or for lint and style nits (use `adk-style`).

skills.name: adk-git
skills.description: Writes commit messages and pull request descriptions for the adk-python repository: Conventional Commits types and scopes, subject lines that say why a change was made, and the linked-issue and testing-plan sections the PR template requires. Use when writing or rewording a commit message, squashing commits before a pull request, drafting a PR description, or checking that a change is shaped to land. Don't use for generic git mechanics such as rebasing, resolving conflicts, cherry-picking, or branch surgery; those need no skill. Don't use to judge the content of a change (use adk-review) or for code style and naming (use adk-style).

skills.name: adk-review
skills.description: Reviews the uncommitted changes in an adk-python working tree and reports correctness, design, public-API stability, test, sample and documentation gaps as a prioritized findings report, fixing them only when asked. Use when the user asks to review local changes, wants a self-review before opening a pull request, asks whether a change breaks the public API or needs tests, samples or docs, or asks what is wrong with the current diff. Required for changes to public APIs, core architecture (Runner, Workflow, BaseNode), new features and major refactors. Don't use for a single style nit (use adk-style), for diagnosing a failing test or a misbehaving agent at runtime (use adk-debug), or for wording a commit message or PR description (use adk-git).

skills.name: adk-style
skills.description: Python style and codebase conventions for ADK (Agent Development Kit): private-by-default file visibility, imports, type hints, Pydantic v2 models, formatting, docstrings, logging, async I/O, file and test layout, and unit test structure. Use when writing or editing ADK source or tests, deciding whether a new file or symbol should be public or private, naming or placing a test file, fixing a formatter, linter, or type-check failure (pyink, isort, ruff, mypy, addlicense, compliance-checks), or asking whether code matches house style. Don't use for reviewing a whole changeset (use adk-review), writing a developer guide or design doc for a code unit (use adk-unit-guide or adk-unit-design), building or configuring agents (use adk-agent-builder), or installing the toolchain (use adk-setup).

skills.name: adk-unit-design
skills.description: Writes an as-built architecture document for one ADK code unit — purpose, execution flow, data flow, cross-class dependencies, extension points, and the parts that must not change — to `docs/design/{topic}/{unit}/index.md`. It describes the code as implemented, not a proposed design, and its reader is a developer about to change or extend that unit. Use when asked to "write a design doc for {file}", "document the architecture of {class}", "document the extension points of {unit}", or after adding a core class, node type, or plugin base. Don't use for documentation aimed at developers who only call the unit from their own application — that is a usage guide with runnable examples under `docs/guides/` (use `adk-unit-guide`). Don't use to answer a framework-wide architecture question (use `adk-architecture`).

skills.name: bigquery-graph
skills.description: Skill for Graph Query Language (GQL) or SQL/PGQ queries against a property graph. Includes path finding, multi-hop traversal, topological connection, shortest path, node reachability, edge connectivity, and semantic graph queries.

skills.name: mirrord-beyond
skills.description: Help users set up and use mirrord Beyond, which runs a local process against workloads outside Kubernetes (docs section "Beyond Kubernetes"; the CLI, dashboard and config call them serverless workloads and `serverless/` targets). Two tracks. ECS setup, for platform teams - wire an existing Amazon ECS service (Fargate or EC2) to the MetalBear Cloud sessions-manager - store the serverless agent API key in AWS Secrets Manager, merge the mirrord remote bootstrap into the task definition, deploy and verify. Developer session - sign in with `mirrord login`, write a `mirrord-up.yaml` with a `serverless/` target, and run `mirrord up` (or the IDE) against the ECS service. Use when users mention mirrord Beyond, Beyond Kubernetes, ECS or Fargate with mirrord, serverless targets, sessions-manager, MetalBear Cloud, the serverless agent API key, MIRRORD_REMOTE_SERVICE, or errors from either side. Also covers the Operator-hosted mode briefly.

skills.name: mirrord-chaos
skills.description: Help users chaos test their app with mirrord: inject artificial latency or connection errors into a mirrord session's outgoing traffic via per-session chaos rules managed with the `mirrord chaos` CLI. skills.name: mirrord-header-propagation
skills.description: Makes a codebase propagate W3C baggage (the `baggage` header carrying `mirrord-session=<key>`) end to end, so mirrord HTTP filters, preview environments, and queue splitting can route a whole request chain to one developer's session. Detects existing OpenTelemetry, Datadog, or other tracing that can already propagate baggage and enables it; otherwise adds a small propagation layer. Covers inbound/outbound HTTP and gRPC, publishing to and consuming from Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS/SNS, GCP Pub/Sub, Azure Service Bus, NATS, Redis Pub/Sub, BullMQ and Temporal, per-message context restore in consumers, and storage hand-offs such as a GCS signed URL upload that triggers Pub/Sub or an S3 presigned upload that triggers SQS. Ends with a report of every flow found and which ones still drop the header. Use when the user asks to propagate headers, baggage, tracestate, the mirrord session key, or trace context across services or queues, or when a mirrord filter matches the first service but not downstream services or queue consumers.

skills.name: alphafold2
skills.description: Predict protein structure for monomers and multimers with AlphaFold2 via the ColabFold runner (Mirdita et al. 2022, github.com/sokrypton/ColabFold; AlphaFold2 Jumper et al. 2021). Reach for this skill to fold a sequence or complex with the AF2/AF2-Multimer evoformer, to validate designed sequences by self-consistency pLDDT, ipTM, and RMSD, or to run a quick MSA-backed prediction using the public MMseqs2 server.

skills.name: boltz
skills.description: Structure prediction for protein, nucleic-acid, and small-molecule complexes with Boltz-2 (Passaro & Wohlwend et al. 2025, github.com/jwohlwend/boltz). Reach for this skill to validate designed binders against a target, to co-fold a protein with a SMILES or CCD ligand, or to get an open-source AlphaFold3 alternative with optional binding-affinity prediction.

skills.name: borzoi
skills.description: Predict genome-wide functional tracks (RNA-seq, CAGE, DNase, ChIP) from DNA sequence with Borzoi. Use this skill when: (1) Scoring the regulatory effect of a variant on expression/accessibility, (2) Generating predicted coverage tracks for a locus, (3) Prioritising non-coding variants by predicted track delta.

skills.name: chai1
skills.description: Structure prediction for protein, nucleic-acid, and small-molecule complexes with the Chai-1 foundation model (Chai Discovery 2024, github.com/chaidiscovery/chai-lab). Reach for this skill to predict an antibody-antigen or protein-ligand complex from a single FASTA, to re-fold designed binders as an AlphaFold-multimer alternative, or to drive co-folding from Python for batched campaigns on a GPU.

skills.name: compute-env-setup
skills.description: Prepare reproducible setup instructions and validate a user-managed named software environment on an Open-Science SSH Compute Host, including direct SSH and Slurm hosts. Use when a remote job needs packages, modules, cache variables, or a repeatable activation that the host does not already provide.

skills.name: customize
skills.description: Use when the user wants to create or manage a Specialist agent or create, revise, publish, or delete a Skill through the conversational `/Customize` entry. Routes Skill work to the internal skill-creator and handles Specialist work through the JavaScript host.agents SDK.

skills.name: diffdock
skills.description: Predict small-molecule binding poses with DiffDock-L (Corso et al. 2023/2024, github.com/gcorso/DiffDock) — blind diffusion docking that places a ligand into a protein pocket without a predefined search box and ranks the samples with a learned confidence model. Reach for this skill to dock a SMILES or SDF against a PDB, to generate ranked 3D poses for a small fragment library, or to get a starting pose for downstream rescoring. DiffDock predicts geometry, not affinity.

skills.name: esmfold2
skills.description: Biohub ESMFold2 / ESMFold2-Fast all-atom co-folding (Candido et al. 2026, github.com/Biohub/esm). Single-sequence and MSA modes; protein, DNA, RNA, ligand (CCD/SMILES), modified residues. FoldBench Ab-Ag 50-55%, PPI 70-77% DockQ-pass. Also covers the ESMC-{300M,600M,6B} protein language models from the same release: masked-LM logits, hidden states, mutation scoring, contact prediction, and the SAE interpretability head. MIT-licensed weights on HuggingFace org `biohub`. Use this skill when: (1) Predicting complex structures with single-sequence input, (2) Validating designed binders with ESMFold2-Fast, (3) Running ESMFold2 with MSA input, (4) Getting ESMC embeddings or per-residue mutation scores, (5) Choosing kernel backend and sampling-step settings for paper-faithful throughput.

skills.name: evo2
skills.description: Score, embed, and generate DNA sequences with Evo 2, a long-context genomic foundation model. Use this skill when: (1) Computing per-nucleotide or per-sequence likelihoods for variant effect scoring, (2) Embedding genomic windows for downstream classification, (3) Generating DNA conditioned on a prefix, (4) Scoring regulatory or coding regions across species.

skills.name: fair-esm2
skills.description: Embed proteins with Meta AI's ESM-2 (`fair-esm` package). Use this skill when: (1) Extracting per-residue or per-sequence embeddings for downstream ML, (2) Masked-LM likelihood / mutation effect scoring, (3) Contact prediction from a sequence.

skills.name: indication-dossier
skills.description: Generate a therapeutic indication dossier. Covers the patient population, epidemiology, disease biology, standard of care, regulatory precedent, and landmark clinical trials.

skills.name: ligandmpnn
skills.description: Inverse-fold a backbone with ligand, nucleic-acid, and metal context using LigandMPNN (Dauparas et al. 2023, github.com/dauparas/LigandMPNN). Reach for this skill to redesign the residues lining a binding pocket around a bound small molecule or cofactor, to design metal-coordinating sites where the geometry must be respected, or to get threaded designed-sequence PDBs out of any MPNN run.

skills.name: openfold3
skills.description: Structure prediction using OpenFold3, an open-weights PyTorch reproduction of AlphaFold3 from the AlQuraishi Lab. Use this skill when predicting protein/nucleic-acid/ligand complex structures with an Apache-2.0-licensed AF3 reimplementation.

skills.name: proteinmpnn
skills.description: Inverse-fold a protein backbone (PDB structure) into amino-acid sequence with ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al. 2022, github.com/dauparas/ProteinMPNN). Reach for this skill to run sequence design on RFdiffusion backbones, to redesign one chain of a PDB while holding interface residues fixed, or to generate a temperature-swept set of sequences for downstream folding.

skills.name: remote-compute-ssh
skills.description: Evaluate and use Remote Compute before choosing where to run GPU, high-memory, parallel, batch, model-inference, bioinformatics, or other long-running scientific work; supports short remote commands and asynchronous jobs with automatic harvest and analysis.

skills.name: scgpt
skills.description: Embed and annotate single-cell expression data with scGPT, a foundation model for single-cell biology. Use this skill when: (1) Producing cell embeddings from an AnnData for clustering/integration, (2) Zero-shot or fine-tuned cell-type annotation, (3) Gene-level representation for perturbation/GRN tasks. For probabilistic single-cell models (scVI etc.), use the scvi-tools library.

skills.name: self-awareness
skills.description: Inspect Open-Science's JavaScript control REPL, discover managed Project files, Sessions, and Agent Frames, and safely feature-gate host.* calls with host.capabilities(). Use when an Agent needs to discover available host APIs, locate an Artifact or Upload Version, diagnose a Session, or read a Frame transcript in the current Project.

skills.name: solublempnn
skills.description: Inverse-fold a backbone with SolubleMPNN — ProteinMPNN retrained on a soluble-PDB subset (Dauparas et al. 2022) — for sequences biased toward cytosolic expression and reduced aggregation. Reach for this skill when designs from vanilla ProteinMPNN are aggregating or going to inclusion bodies, when redesigning a membrane-adjacent fold for soluble expression, or when an E. coli expression screen is the next step.

Check the governance rules for this task

skills.name: add-product-e2e-eval
skills.description: Add or extend a Paperclip full-stack runner E2E workflow, fixture, matcher, or report evidence path for local or Daytona execution.
